title: Flyweight, and why to avoid Singletons
summary: Share heavy data; pass dependencies in.

cards.title: Flyweight
cards.body: Ten thousand trees, one mesh. The per-tree data is only what differs: position, scale and a pointer to the shared model. The sizes shown are real `sizeof` values on this phone.

cards.title: The Singleton problem
cards.body: A Singleton is a global with a nicer name. Any function can depend on it invisibly, and tests can't replace it. Passing the dependency in (`SpinButton(Audio&)`) makes it visible, and the tests in this repo hand in a fake `Audio` to check the button.

cards.question: What does the flyweight version store per tree?
choices: A full copy of the mesh
Only what differs (position, scale) plus a pointer to shared data
cards.explain: That's the whole idea: intrinsic data is shared once, extrinsic data lives in each instance.
